Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (current impression): Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare.
- Relevant differential diagnoses and reasoning (aligned with transcript data):
  - Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate likelihood: acute onset over days with pruritus and multi-site involvement; trigger diary recommended to identify exposures.
  - Irritant contact dermatitis — Moderate likelihood: very dry, cracked skin with redness and itching; could be exacerbated by washing/shower products.

Management Plan

- Medications and treatments (dose/route/frequency not documented where not specified):
  - Topical corticosteroid: Stronger potency prescribed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Emollients: Regular use recommended; to be used in bath/shower; specifics not documented.
  - Antihistamines for itch: Loratadine or Piriton recommended; oral dose/frequency not documented; Fexofenadine offered as alternative.
- Procedures or tests: Not indicated at this visit beyond skin-care regimen and monitoring.
- Education and lifestyle recommendations:
  - Maintain a daily skin-care diary to identify potential triggers (products, soaps, shower gels, fabrics, etc.).
  - Continue emollient use and corticosteroid as directed; reassess in 7–10 days if not improved.
  - Consider using a diary to monitor response to an antihistamine; trial a different antihistamine if needed (e.g., Fexofenadine).
- Follow-up and referrals:
  - Follow-up appointment in 7–10 days to evaluate response to therapy.
  - Not recorded: Allied health referral; sexual health clinic referral; mental health support; CTG registration; preventive health follow-up.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Atopic dermatitis (eczema flare)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Known history of eczema; severe pruritus with chest/hands/elbows involvement; acute flare presentation; prior partial response to steroids aligns with current management (steroid + emollients).
- Allergic contact dermatitis
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Acute onset after several days with multi-site itching; trigger exposure possible but not clearly identified; diary recommended to clarify.
- Irritant contact dermatitis
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Very dry/cracked skin and intense itch with possible irritant exposure (frequent washing or products) consistent with dermatitis.
- Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma)
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Chronic pruritic dermatosis can mimic eczema, but acute onset over days makes this unlikely; considered but not favored given current data.
